newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Global media group raps Belgrade radio crackdown.
newsitem.headline: Global media group raps Belgrade radio crackdown.

text.p: A global network of editors and publishers on Tuesday condemned the closure of an independent Belgrade radio station amid an unprecendented wave of opposition protests in Yugoslavia.
In London the British government also deplored the decision to close the station, and called on the authorities in Belgrade to reconsider it.

The Vienna-based International Press Institute (IPI) said in an open letter to Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic that his decision to shut down the radio, one of a handful of independent stations in Serbia, was a grave violation of the U.N. Declaration of Human Rights/
"(IPI) strongly condemns the closing of Radio B-92," said the letter, a copy of which was made available to Reuters.

"We...urge Your Excellency to ensure that Radio B-92 is allowed to resume operating and that the country's independent media is free to report on events currently taking place in Serbia," said the IPI, which represents media in 80 countries.

The transmitter used by Radio B-92, which unlike state broadcasters has give wide coverage to opposition demonstrations that have swept the capital and other Yugoslav cities for 16 days, was switched off at 3 p.m. (1400 GMT) on Tuesday, radio staff said.
The demonstrators are protesting over Milosevic's decision to annul local elections last month won by opposition candidates in Belgrade and other cities.
Over the past two weeks, the radio has repeatedly complained its signal was being jammed, and has begun sending news over the Internet in both Serbo-Croat and English.
Britain said on Tuesday it deplored the closure of an independent Belgrade radio station and urged the Serbian authorities to reopen it.
"We deplore the decision by the federal authorities to declare Radio B-92 illegal and to prevent it from broadcasting," a Foreign Office spokeswoman said.
"We urge the authorities to reverse their decision. It is important at this moment for independent democratic voices to be heard."

Diplomatic sources in London said a conference in the British capital this week to take stock of the year-old Bosnian peace process would give major Western powers a chance to express their displeasure to the Serbian leadership.
